info.title: release-notes: a dotnet tool to generate release notes from GitHub
info.description: Generate release notes from closed github issues and PR's through the power of version labels

commands.name: apply-labels
commands.description: Creates the version and backport labels for the next release.

options.name: --help
options.description: Show help.

options.name: --version
options.description: Version that is being released.

options.name: --token
options.description: The GitHub token to use. If the issue list is long this may be necessary; defaults to anonymous. [default: null]

options.name: --old-version
options.description: The previous version to generate release notes since. Optional; the tool will find the previous release. [default: null]

options.name: --release-tag-format
options.description: The release tag format. VERSION is replaced by the actual version. [default: VERSION]

options.name: --release-label-format
options.description: The release label format. VERSION is replaced by the actual version. [default: vVERSION]

options.name: --backport-label-format
options.description: The backport label format, e.g. "Backport BRANCH". BRANCH is calculated from the version. [default: null]

options.name: --format
options.description:
The format in which to print the results: Markdown or AsciiDoc. [default: 0]
One of: <markdown|asciidoc>

options.name: --uncategorized-header
options.description: The header to use in the markdown for uncategorized issues/PRs. [default: null]

options.name: --label
options.description:
[repeatable] Map a GitHub label to a categorization heading, formatted as <label>=<description>. May be given
more than once. Defaults to bug=Bug Fixes, enhancement=New Features, documentation=Documentation Improvements. [default: null]

options.name: --output
options.description: Write the release notes to a file as well as standard out. VERSION is replaced by the actual version. [default: null]

commands.name: create-release
commands.description:
Makes sure the tag exists as a release on GitHub, and
introduces new version labels for the next major/minor/patch.
